chapter: Louis Metcalf and leading his own bands
title: Leading bands for Masonic balls and giving sidemen solos
summary: Through the Masonic fraternity he led groups from four to sixteen pieces, using stock arrangements and letting every man take solos.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah, well, that's -- after that I went into the masonic fraternity, you know, all order them, by being a musician, and they gave something like the Shriners, they have this big potentates ball, boatride and this and that. So that's what kept me up on my horn. I'd have six, seven gigs a month. I'd have Flood on trumpet, different ones.
What would you do? Sort of have different size bands or --
Some I played from four pieces up to 15 or 16.
According to what they new worked,
According to what the hall required. I had 16 pieces down at this -- at the New York Hilton Hotel many times, Americana.
Well, what would these bands -- I mean what would you use there, stocks or --
You got arrangements that you'd gathered up during the years?
Yeah, that's true. I had arrangements, all different parts, you know.
Well, I mean did you -- when you were leaving your own groups, I mean were you sort of featuring yourself on tenor or were you sort of acting as the conductor more, or both (unintelligible)?
I was more or less asked (unintelligible) was the any man leader, and I always would feature (unintelligible) in my band. I would let them play solos.

Any men in my band, that I wanted to play solos I would let them play solos, because the funny thing they'd say, well, you're a peculiar guy to lead. I said, why? "Because you give more incentive to a guy playing a solo, if it's a tenor solo or what, and inspire you?" I said, that's right. That's why I let them play solos, whatever they want to play. But I broke (unintelligible) Tiny Bradshaw to that, and we had four men, two featured altos, two tenors, so Tiny wanted me to be leader. I said, he wants to play some too. Let him play a solo. That's what it was. You get better cooperation.
(Unintelligible) said, I'm not going to be no one man band. I'm paying them.
